sources.title: Fresh isolated source-first top-students SQL review

claims.text: The source requires ranking by count of subjects at 80 or above and displaying student name plus passed-subject count, while schema, pass threshold, tie semantics and multiple-attempt policy are not preserved source facts.
The candidate explicitly adopts a minimal students/scores schema, one final score per student/subject, a parameterized pass threshold and deterministic exact-three ROW_NUMBER tie semantics.
Writer and independent reviewer fixtures verify student-grain aggregation, the >=80 boundary, exact-three deterministic ties and independence of the passed-subject metric from the ranking metric.

validation.command: extract exact SQL candidate and execute independent SQLite adversarial fixture with two pass-score bindings
validation.reported_stdout: PASS exact_candidate student-grain >=80-boundary exact-three stable-tie pass-score-independent
checks: exact SQL candidate parses and executes
conditional aggregation occurs at student grain before ranking
score exactly 80 counts under the declared >=80 interpretation
ROW_NUMBER plus student_id gives deterministic exact-three output under the declared tie contract
changing pass_score changes displayed passed_subjects independently from the >=80 ranking metric

boundary_tests.expected: 80 counts toward high-score subject count under declared >=80 contract

boundary_tests.case: Cara and Eve tie at three high-score subjects
boundary_tests.expected: student_id tie-break deterministically orders Cara then Eve while returning exactly three students
Alice passed_subjects changes from 3 to 2 while ranking by >=80 count is unchanged
does not enter top three when higher student aggregates exist

findings: The repository source preserves ranking students by count of subjects at 80 or above and displaying name plus passed-subject count, but it does not preserve schema names, the pass threshold, tie semantics, or multiple-attempt policy.

The candidate explicitly labels those missing details as answer-side assumptions: a minimal students/scores schema, one final row per student/subject, a bound :pass_score, and exact-three ROW_NUMBER semantics with student_id as tie-breaker.
The exact SQL independently executes successfully and ranks only after student-level conditional aggregation; the 80-point inclusive boundary is covered by a dedicated case.
Changing pass_score from 60 to 75 changes the displayed pass count without changing the >=80 ranking metric, proving the two conditions are not conflated.
The answer explains the DENSE_RANK alternative if the interviewer instead intends the top three ranks with all ties, and it refuses to invent retry/retake semantics or production experience.
